einzeiler: Eric Holder on preparing to protect the midterms from election interference.
kurzfassung: Former Attorney General Eric Holder discusses the legal and strategic preparations being made to counter potential federal interference in the upcoming midterms. He details tabletop exercises, court strategies, and the importance of voter turnout and grassroots action. Despite unprecedented challenges from the administration, Holder expresses confidence in the resilience of American democratic institutions.
stichpunkte: Holder criticizes the Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security for actions designed to sow doubt and intimidate voters.
Legal teams have pre-filed court documents and prepared writs of mandamus to swiftly challenge any refusal to certify election results.
Holder and other civil society leaders have conducted tabletop exercises to game out and prepare responses to various doomsday scenarios.
Federal law explicitly prohibits armed federal agents or military personnel near polling places.
The administration's attempts to use the intelligence community and DHS for domestic ballot seizures are criticized as unprecedented overreach.
Despite partisan gerrymandering efforts, coordinated legal battles and public protests have largely dismantled Republican map-redrawing schemes.
Public education regarding civics, gerrymandering, and election mechanics has increased significantly during the Trump administration.
Holder emphasizes that massive voter turnout and peaceful public protest remain the ultimate antidotes to subversion attempts.
beschreibung:
Former Attorney General Eric Holder joins Alex Wagner to game out the ways Trump might try to steal the midterms, from weaponizing the Department of Justice, to sending Homeland Security after suspected noncitizen voters, to straight-up misinformation and intimidation. They talk about how Democrats are preparing to fight back, what Holder has learned running election war games with Hillary Clinton, and why listeners need to lock in their voting plan. Then, Holder, chairman of the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, explains why GOP gerrymandering efforts ahead of the midterms have—hopefully—fallen flat, and why the battle against partisan maps will continue into 2028 and beyond.
